text:
Sam: Heads-up — customer 'orchid' on Dedicated pool dp-42 hitting repeated 429s since yesterday evening. They moved from a trial plan to reserved last night.
Maria: Tenant ID? sample request ids?
Sam: tenant=orchid, sample req IDs: r-93a1, r-93a2. Repro curl I ran: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'X-Tenant: orchid' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` -> 429 with body `{"error":"rate_exceeded","limit":0}`
Alex: I pulled logs from rate-translator for orchid around those req IDs. see trace: ```[2025-01-18T22:03:12Z] tenant=orchid plan=reserved42 translated_units=0 reason=quota-override source=plan-merge``` Looks like the plan merge step set the effective ceiling to 0 during a config roll.
Jess: We did a plan-tag migration for reserved plans last night — could be related. Maria, any chance the denom conversion (minutes->hours) was applied twice?
Maria: Good call. There was a migration script that normalizes `rate_unit_denom`. If a tenant already had a normalized value the upsert path was accidentally doubling the divisor. That would make a previously nonzero ceiling evaluate to 0.
Sam: Customer impact: steady 429s across all routes on dp-42, high latency from queueing. They flagged as P1.
sre-bot: Incident created INC-5621 and paging oncall @alex.
Alex: Quick repro on my side: `GET /quota/effective?tenant=orchid` -> `{"effective_units":0, "source":"plan:reserved42"}` Logs indicate `merge_policy` used `overwrite` instead of `max` for `ceiling_seconds` in one code path.
Jess: I'll pull the migration diff. (checking) — yep, in `migrations/2025-01-rate-denom.sql` we do `UPDATE quotas SET denom = denom * 60 WHERE ...`, but the application layer also applied denom conversion on the upsert path. Double conversion.
Maria: Temporary mitigation: we can patch translator to treat any computed effective_units <= 0 as fallback to legacy ceil (take previous value) while we fix data. Alex, could you hotfix?
Alex: On it. Plan: 1) roll translator hotfix (treat <=0 as suspicious) 2) run safe backfill to recompute effective quotas for affected tenants 3) invalidate quota cache on dp-42 nodes.
Sam: Steps to reproduce for support engineers: 1) run repro curl above 2) `curl -sS https://api.redwood.example/internal/quota/tenant/orchid | jq` 3) verify `effective_units`==0 4) capture translator logs with `service=rate-translator` and grep for `plan-merge`.
Jess: I can take customer comms once we have hotfix ETA.
Alex: Hotfix deployed to canary within 8m. Patch shows translator now logs a warning instead of forcing 0 and uses previous cached value. Example log: ```[WARN] computed_effective_units<=0 for tenant=orchid, using cached=720000```
Sam: After canary pass, I triggered backfill for orchard of dp-42: `POST /internal/quota/recompute?tenant=orchid` -> job id job-773.
Maria: Backfill job finished, recomputed effective_units -> 720000, cache invalidated across dp-42.
Sam: Customer confirmed reduced 429s and normal latency. Jess, sent update to them.
Jess: Customer acknowledged and will monitor for 24h. I noted RCA and mitigation in INC-5621.
Alex: Long-term fix: we'll adjust migration to be idempotent and change merge policy from `overwrite` to `max` for ceilings. I'll file a PR and schedule a release.
Sam: Thanks team. Closing loop: ensure we scan for tenants with `effective_units<=1` across all pools and run safe backfill.
Jess: +1. Marking support ticket resolved pending 24h observation. :white_check_mark:
